recentItems.title: ‘Never sell love for money’: China actress Jing Tian hits back at crypto mogul Justin Sun
recentItems.description:

Chinese cryptocurrency tycoon Justin Sun is suing actress Jing Tian and her parents to recover a “bride price” of 30 million yuan (US$4.5 million). Sun has also published a post titled “My Girlfriend Jing Tian,” recounting their relationship and touching on surrogacy and the payment. He has labelled the account “fictional,” waived copyright and invited its circulation online.

recentItems.title: Orangutan rescued from Borneo wildfires
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

A sick orangutan has been found in the Indonesian village of Ketapang, a victim of forest fires sweeping Borneo island. A wildlife foundation rushed a veterinarian to the scene to treat the animal, which was suffering from respiratory illness. The worsening smoke haze has pushed Indonesia to intensify efforts to contain the fires across Borneo and Sumatra.

recentItems.title: Nepal digs mass graves for unidentified flood victims
recentItems.description:
Nepali authorities have converted a forest in the scenic Chitwan district into a temporary burial ground for unidentified victims of last week’s devastating flash floods. Authorities said DNA samples were collected from each body and the gravesites were carefully recorded, allowing for remains to be exhumed if the deceased can be identified later. Meanwhile, search and rescue efforts in Nepal have increasingly focused on freeing hundreds of workers believed to be trapped in tunnels linked to several major hydropower projects.

recentItems.title: Crowds visit Hong Kong bookstore set to close after police raid
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

An independent Hong Kong bookstore that has shut its doors six weeks after a national security police raid, drew long queues of customers on its final day. As the Have a Nice Stay bookstore wrapped up four years in business on Sunday afternoon, the queues wound through a dim staircase in a Prince Edward tenement building as some customers waited up to 45 minutes to enter the third-floor shop. The closure followed a mid-July operation by national security officers, who raided the shop alongside nearby Greenfield Bookstore over allegations of acts with seditious intent.

recentItems.title: Where are China’s youth headed in a crowded job market?
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

China this year saw a record 12.7 million fresh university graduates, who now face an uphill battle securing stable work in an already crowded job market. Since 2020, China’s youth unemployment has been a persistent problem, forcing many young Chinese to seek work in the public sector for “iron rice bowl” jobs. Others are opting for postgraduate study to boost their future prospects or defer entering the workforce. But many have also been relying on gig work to make ends meet.

recentItems.title: Chinese rescuers repair critical road to disaster-hit border port
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

Rescuers on Saturday restored the first sharp-curve section on China’s national highway G216, preparing for full reopening of the critical lifeline to the disaster-hit border port of Gyirong in Tibet. The road had been completely destroyed by the flash flood caused by a high-altitude glacial collapse in Nepal on August 26. The torrent of water, ice, rock and debris slammed into Gyirong port and caused widespread damage as it moved downstream.

recentItems.title: Drone footage shows extent of damage in Nepal village after disaster
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

Get the latest: https://sc.mp/a3e99e

The village of Devighat in Nepal’s Nuwakot district was among the worst hit by the flash flood disaster on August 26. Video taken from a drone 3 days later showed the extent of damage. Scientists who studied satellite images said bedrock underneath a glacier high in the Himalayan region had collapsed, taking part of the glacier with it. The rockfall was so extreme that it registered as magnitude 5.2. The rocks and melted water then swelled the rivers in the valleys below, causing a torrent of water that swept buildings, bridges and earth downstream in Tibet and Nepal.

recentItems.title: How an American teacher and Chinese farmer grew a forest in the desert
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

In 1999, American teacher Ronald Sakolsky raised US$5,000 to help Inner Mongolian farmer Yin Yuzhen fight desertification by planting trees in northern China’s Mu Us Desert. Twenty-six years later, they reunited to walk through a thriving green forest that replaced the barren sands.
